summary: Exact open interval in a on which the same 42 offsets, hence the same 888 edges and identical 6-UNSAT certificate, apply: a in (1/sqrt28, 1/sqrt19) = (0.188982, 0.229416), containing 1/5 with margins 0.0110 and 0.0294; rational closed subinterval [0.19, 0.22] with exact integer margins (361*28 = 10108 > 10000; 484*19 = 9196 < 10000). Derivation: the configuration at a is the homothety image of that at a = 1, so dmin(v,a) = a*mu(v), dmax(v,a) = a*nu(v), and strict forcing is 1/nu(v) < a < 1/mu(v); intersecting over the 42 offsets gives (1/min nu, 1/max mu). Per-ring values exact in Q(sqrt3), constant per ring (checked): ring 4 gives nu^2 = 28 (lower endpoint), ring 13 gives mu^2 = 19 (upper). The 888 edges realise exactly these 42 offsets and the edge condition does not mention a, so the CNF and the 42109-step refutation are the same file throughout. Cross-checked WITHOUT homothety by direct recomputation at 0.188, 19/100, 1/5, 11/50, 0.23: fails just outside at exactly the ring-4 and ring-13 offsets. Endpoints excluded as tangencies. Strict interior distances avoid boundary ownership. Family exclusion at six colours only, not a chromatic bound; chi = 8 uncertified and unused.

Homothety: dmin(v,a) = a*dmin(v,1) and dmax(v,a) = a*dmax(v,1); v strictly forced at a iff 1/nu(v) < a < 1/mu(v); all 42 offsets stay strictly forced exactly on the open interval (1/min nu, 1/max mu).
verified_results.grade: PROOF (homothety plus finite intersection of strict inequalities)

verified_results.statement: Exact per-ring values at a = 1 in Q(sqrt3), constant on each ring (verified, not assumed): N=4: mu^2=3, nu^2=28; N=7: 7,43; N=9: 12,49; N=12: 16,64; N=13: 19,67. Hence max mu^2 = 19 (ring 13) and min nu^2 = 28 (ring 4).

escalation: Precise obstacle for the record: the interval (1/sqrt28, 1/sqrt19) is certified for the SAME 42 offsets, but its two endpoints are limits of that particular witness set, not of the phenomenon. Below 1/sqrt28 the ring-4 offsets stop being forced (dmax < 1, the cells drift apart); above 1/sqrt19 ring 13 stops being forced (dmin > 1). Extending the interval in either direction requires a different offset set, hence a fresh 6-colouring CNF and a fresh refutation, and the lower direction is the harder one: there the forced offsets are an annulus around distance 1 rather than a ball, which is exactly where the earlier census found the 7-clique method dead. Expected useful output: a 6-UNSAT patch at a parameter below 1/sqrt28, or a proof that no ball patch of <= 81 cells can be 6-UNSAT below that threshold.
